discovery: Discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos with the IceCube Neutrino Observatory
motivation: Francis Halzen conceived the kilometre-scale neutrino telescope in the Antarctic ice and led its realisation, from AMANDA to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory. In 2013 IceCube discovered a flux of high-energy neutrinos of extraterrestrial origin, with energies up to several PeV, opening an entirely new window on the Universe. Neutrinos are ideal astrophysical messengers: they travel undeflected by magnetic fields and unabsorbed by matter, pointing back to the most violent cosmic accelerators. The discovery was followed by the first identified sources: the blazar TXS 0506+056 in a multi-messenger campaign (2017-2018), the active galaxy NGC 1068 (2022), and the Galactic plane in neutrinos (2023). The idea of instrumenting a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice sounded simple, but implementing it was a formidable technical achievement. This is a clearly identified discovery that established neutrino astronomy as a new field of observational physics.
